# The working life of Simargl: from the myths to the modern trades

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Simargl** works now.

Simargl has no mythology in the ordinary sense — no tale was ever told about him. He exists as a single line in a chronicle, a name of Iranian ancestry, and a century of scholarly argument about what a winged guardian was doing in a Slavic pantheon.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Simargl
- **Pantheon:** Slavic
- **Domain of influence:** Winged Guardian, Plant Life
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 447 of 546

## The Myth at Work

**The Idols in the Dnieper.** In 988 the Primary Chronicle's procession of drowned gods includes, between Stribog and Mokosh, a name no Slavic tongue built: Simargl.  The chronicler lists him without curiosity, one idol among six, but modern scholarship has never been able to leave him alone — because his name betrays a long journey, from the Iranian Simurgh, through the speech of steppe peoples who traded and raided along the Black Sea, into the capital of Christianizing Rus'. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**A Name from Persia.** The Simurgh of Iranian tradition is one of the oldest great birds of world mythology.  In the Avesta she roosts in the branches of the sacred tree; across Sogdian and Sasanian art she spreads composite wings over the Tree of Life; and in Ferdowsi's Shahnameh she rears the hero Zal and guides his son Rostam through every impossible task — part dog, part lion, part bird, and wholly wise. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*Primary seat: Simargl embodies winged guardian, plant life — the core of agriculture food.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Simargl performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Environmental & Climate Services

*Climate science, ecology, and sustainability consulting. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*Resonant seat: Simargl shares symbolic territory with environment climate.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

## The Long Employment

Simargl's legacy divides in two.  Among Iranists he is a footnote in the biography of the Simurgh — evidence of how far the great bird's name flew, from Avestan hymns to a chronicle on the Dnieper. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

The atlas is not a horoscope. Seats are earned from the sources — argued, weighted, published — and every one of them can be challenged at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). A match that cannot survive an argument does not survive review. That is the whole trick: the patterns are claims, and claims can be tested.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/simargl/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
